base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a cell phone plan and get set up. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I need to pick a new cell phone plan. I've narrowed it down to 3 options from different carriers.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 cell phone plans: Plan A (Premium Plus from CarrierOne), Plan B (Standard Pro from CarrierTwo), Plan C (Essential from CarrierThree)

Plan A: unlimited data, 5G priority, hotspot 50GB, international roaming included — $95/month. Plan B: 30GB data, 5G access, hotspot 15GB, no international roaming — $55/month. Plan C: 15GB data, 4G LTE, hotspot 5GB, no international roaming — $30/month
Employer reimburses up to $40/month for cell phone expenses, user pays the rest out of pocket
User can only afford to spend $15/month out of pocket on top of the employer reimbursement
User mostly uses WiFi at home and at the office, does not stream video on mobile, mainly needs data for maps and messaging on the go

constraints.value: Maximum total monthly spend on phone plan is $55 (employer $40 + personal $15), so any plan above $55/month is eliminated
constraints.surface_form: My company covers up to 40 bucks a month for phone bills, and personally I can chip in maybe 15 on top of that — just moved to a new apartment so money is tight

constraints.value: User does not need unlimited or large data plans — light mobile data user who is mostly on WiFi
constraints.surface_form: I'm on WiFi pretty much all day — at home and at the office. I really just need data for Google Maps and WhatsApp when I'm out
inference_chain: On WiFi at home and office → most hours covered by WiFi
Only uses maps and messaging on mobile → very low mobile data consumption
Does not need unlimited data or large data allotment → Plan A's unlimited data is unnecessary overkill

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 cell phone plans (A, B, C). You will share plan details, your employer reimbursement amount, and your personal budget across several turns. Your colleague and friend will praise Plans A and B. At the very end, you will simply say you have made your decision and need to sign up this week, asking which plan you should go with — you must NEVER name which plan you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person. You never express frustration or impatience. You treat each piece of information as normal conversation. When mentioning friends or colleagues, you are casually sharing what you heard, not asking for advice about their plans.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could cause identity confusion or answer leakage

aims.description: I need to pick a new cell phone plan. I've narrowed it down to 3 options from different carriers.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the phone plan selection

aims.description: So here's what I'm looking at. Plan A is Premium Plus from CarrierOne — unlimited data, 5G priority, 50GB hotspot, international roaming, $95 a month. Plan B is Standard Pro from CarrierTwo — 30GB data, 5G, 15GB hotspot, no international roaming, $55 a month. And Plan C is Essential from CarrierThree — 15GB data, 4G LTE, 5GB hotspot, no international roaming, $30 a month.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 plans with their prices and features
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 plans with prices and features in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague at work just switched to Plan A last month. He keeps raving about how fast the 5G is and how the hotspot saved him during a power outage at his place.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Plan A experience

drift_config.drift_topic: switched to Plan A, loves the 5G speed and hotspot reliability during a power outage

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Plan A

aims.description: My company covers up to 40 bucks a month for phone bills, and personally I can chip in maybe 15 on top of that — just moved to a new apartment so money is tight
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the combined budget cap of $55/month ($40 employer + $15 personal) and ideally recognizes Plan A ($95) is eliminated
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — employer $40 + personal $15 = $55 cap, eliminates Plan A ($95)

aims.description: My colleague also mentioned Plan A includes free international roaming — he went to Mexico last month and didn't pay a cent extra. Said it was seamless.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the international roaming benefit of Plan A

drift_config.drift_topic: used Plan A's free international roaming in Mexico, seamless experience

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Plan A (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I'm on WiFi pretty much all day — at home and at the office. I really just need data for Google Maps and WhatsApp when I'm out.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes the user has very light mobile data needs, making Plan B's 30GB unnecessary
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver data usage constraint — light user on WiFi most of the day, 15GB is more than enough

aims.description: My friend just signed up for Plan B actually. She works in sales and is out on the road a lot — she told me the 30GB has been perfect for her, never runs out.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Plan B experience

drift_config.drift_topic: signed up for Plan B, works in sales on the road, 30GB is perfect for her usage

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Plan B

aims.description: She also said CarrierTwo has really good customer service — she had a billing issue and they sorted it out in like ten minutes on the phone.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive CarrierTwo customer service review

drift_config.drift_topic: CarrierTwo has great customer service, resolved billing issue in ten minutes

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Plan B (at budget boundary, but unnecessary data for user)

aims.description: I need to decide and sign up this week. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends Plan C ($30/month) as the clear choice — it is well within the $55 budget ($40 employer + $15 personal), and 15GB is more than enough for the user's light data needs (WiFi at home and office, only maps and messaging on mobile). Plan A ($95) is $40 over budget. Plan B ($55) is right at the cap but offers 30GB the user does not need, wasting money on unnecessary capacity when Plan C covers the use case at nearly half the price.
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to a specific plan based on constraints

ground_truth.answer: The user should sign up for Plan C (Essential from CarrierThree, $30/month). Plan A ($95/month) far exceeds the $55 combined budget ($40 employer reimbursement + $15 personal). Plan B ($55/month) sits exactly at the budget ceiling but provides 30GB of data the user does not need — the user is on WiFi at home and at the office and only uses maps and messaging on mobile, making 15GB more than sufficient. Plan C ($30/month) is well within budget and matches the user's actual data needs.
required_elements: Agent recommends Plan C specifically as the plan to sign up for
Agent shows that Plan A at $95/month exceeds the derived $55/month cap from $40 employer reimbursement plus $15 personal budget
Agent shows that Plan B at $55/month hits the budget ceiling while providing 30GB data the user does not need given WiFi coverage at home and office
Agent shows that Plan C at $30/month fits within the $55 combined budget and that 15GB is sufficient for the user's light mobile usage of maps and messaging
forbidden_elements: Recommending Plan A ($95/month exceeds the $55 combined budget by $40)
Recommending Plan B without acknowledging the user's light data usage makes 30GB unnecessary and Plan C a better value
Ignoring the employer reimbursement cap of $40 when computing the total affordable amount
Ignoring the personal budget limit of $15 when computing the total affordable amount
Asking the user which plan they decided on instead of computing the answer from constraints
Treating Plan B as the best choice solely because it matches the budget ceiling without considering data needs
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: employer reimburses $40/month + user can add $15/month = $55/month total cap. Plan A ($95) exceeds cap by $40 — eliminated. Plan B ($55) is at the cap but provides 30GB data the user does not need (on WiFi at home and office, only uses maps and messaging on mobile — 15GB is plenty). Plan C ($30) is well within budget and matches actual usage. Data usage constraint: user is a light mobile data user on WiFi most of the day. 15GB from Plan C is more than sufficient. 30GB from Plan B is unnecessary overkill. Despite 4 drift turns praising Plan A (colleague's 5G speed, hotspot, international roaming) and Plan B (friend's 30GB usage, CarrierTwo customer service), the agent must respect the hard budget constraint and the user's stated light data needs to recommend Plan C.

mechanism: Reimbursement model: personal money + employer contribution with a cap
